claims.text: Prolapse is staged on examination with the POP-Q system.
claims.quote: Severity of pelvic organ prolapse can be staged by the Pelvic Organ Prolapse-Quantification ( POP-Q ) system

claims.text: Incontinence labs: urinalysis, urine culture, and kidney function (creatinine, estimated GFR).
claims.quote: Urinalysis, urine culture, and assessment of kidney function (serum creatinine and estimated GFR) are required.

claims.text: Postvoid residual by ultrasound (preferred) or catheter: < 50 mL is normal; > 100 mL may mean detrusor underactivity or outlet obstruction.
claims.quote: Postvoid residual volume should be determined by ultrasound (preferred) or catheterization. Postvoid residual volume plus voided volume estimates total bladder capacity and helps assess bladder proprioception. A postvoid residual volume < 50 mL is normal; a volume < 100 mL is usually acceptable in patients > 65 years but abnormal in younger patients and one > 100 mL may suggest detrusor underactivity or outlet obstruction.

claims.text: Urodynamic testing when the evaluation isn't diagnostic or before surgery.
claims.quote: Urodynamic testing is indicated when clinical evaluation combined with the appropriate tests is not diagnostic or when abnormalities must be precisely characterized before surgery.
